sources.title: Zambia: Drought Response Appeal May 2024 - December 2024
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Zambia and OCHA
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023/2024 rainfall-season drought impacts and response outlook, as reported in May 2024.
sources.methodology: UN appeal page summarizes government crop assessment, meteorological and IPC information available in May 2024.
sources.limitations: Appeal-era figures and anticipated risks are dated; provincial and assessed-district totals do not identify local causal incidents.

sources.title: Zambia Country Office Humanitarian Situation Report - 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF Zambia humanitarian needs and programme reporting for 2025, including lingering effects of the 2023/2024 drought.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual report of humanitarian needs and programme outputs.
sources.limitations: National and programme aggregates; limited district attribution and independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Post-Implementation Beneficiary Satisfaction and Protection Monitoring Survey
sources.organization: UNICEF Zambia, with the University of Zambia and government partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Cross-sectional perceptions of assistance delivered during the 2023/2024 drought and floods, collected in 2025.
sources.methodology: Mixed-methods survey and focus groups with 950 assistance recipients; descriptive district comparisons.
sources.limitations: Programme-area recipients; summary lists eight districts, methods seven.

sources.title: New Beginnings for Farming Families Rebuilding After Drought in Zambia
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO and partner drought-recovery activities and participant accounts reported in March 2026; effects of the 2023/2024 drought and 2025/2026 rains.
sources.methodology: FAO feature describing programme outputs and accounts from participating farmers and officials.
sources.limitations: Programme feature, not an independent evaluation; participant examples do not estimate prevalence or impact.

sources.title: Rebuilding Hope After the Lundazi Floods
sources.temporal_coverage: Accounts of heavy-rainfall floods beginning in late December 2025 and UNICEF response reported in January 2026.
sources.methodology: UNICEF field feature based on programme reporting and named household accounts in flood-affected districts.
sources.limitations: Human-interest and response account; named household testimony is illustrative, not representative, and response impact is not independently evaluated.

claims.locator: UN in Zambia appeal page, opening drought-impact paragraphs, 8 May 2024.
claims.paraphrase: The 2023/2024 season’s late onset, dry spells and heat affected crops and livestock; over nine million people in 84 of 117 districts were affected, with Central, Eastern, Southern and Western provinces hardest hit.
claims.limitations: May 2024 assessment; provincial totals do not give district-level differences.

claims.locator: UN in Zambia appeal page, protection-risk and child-marriage paragraphs, 8 May 2024.
claims.paraphrase: The appeal warned that drought-related water scarcity could lengthen water-collection journeys and heighten violence, exploitation and abuse risks for women and children; it said drought stress could raise child marriage in some hotspot districts.
claims.scenario: Appeal-era anticipated risks during the 2023/2024 drought response; no climate scenario specified.
claims.limitations: Anticipated risks in a 2024 appeal, not measured incidence; hotspot districts are not named.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The appeal says water scarcity from drought may increase protection risks, including violence and child marriage.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: UN in Zambia appeal page, protection-risk and child-marriage paragraphs, 8 May 2024.

claims.paraphrase: The 2023/2024 drought affected over nine million people in more than 70% of 117 districts; over three million children were food insecure and more than 51,000 faced severe-wasting risk.
claims.limitations: National child totals are not district-disaggregated.

claims.paraphrase: In 2025, UNICEF rehabilitated 86 boreholes (34 at health facilities) in drought-affected districts, benefiting 21,500; a separate cholera response restored water to 4,108 through seven boreholes.
claims.limitations: Districts are unnamed; beneficiary totals refer to separate activities.

claims.paraphrase: The Drought Emergency Cash Transfer used Zambia’s Social Cash Transfer system, assisting over 2.2 million households; UNICEF says it helped families avoid asset sales through district and community delivery.
institutions: Ministry of Community Development and Social Services
claims.limitations: UNICEF annual reporting; aggregate includes regular and emergency beneficiaries.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. iii, executive-summary key findings; methodology printed pp. 2–4.
claims.paraphrase: Among 950 surveyed assistance recipients, 66.7% said aid met household priorities; 27.3% disagreed, citing unmet needs, exclusion or access barriers.
claims.limitations: Recipient perceptions, not evaluated impact; summary lists eight districts, methods seven.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 10, ‘Perceptions of Humanitarian Services Addressing Protection Risks by District.’
claims.paraphrase: Agreement that assistance addressed protection risks was highest in Lunga (87.4%) and lowest in Gwembe (53.2%); authors cite remoteness, roads and communications as constraints.
claims.limitations: Results list eight districts; methods name seven, leaving denominators unclear.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. iii, executive-summary key findings.
claims.paraphrase: Among respondents, 42.3% felt excluded from decisions and 12.4% reported discrimination or access barriers; 87% reported no barriers.
geographies: selected drought- and flood-affected districts in Zambia

claims.locator: FAO feature, opening paragraphs on Gwembe and Sinazongwe drought recovery.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that drought-damaged crops, dried water sources and livestock losses persisted in Gwembe and Sinazongwe after above-average 2025/2026 rains supported crop recovery; some households entered later seasons with depleted herds and assets.
claims.limitations: FAO feature reports programme and participant context, not representative household prevalence.

claims.locator: FAO feature, intervention description and sustainability paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: FAO and partners distributed 1,312 goats to vulnerable farmers in Gwembe and Sinazongwe, reporting about 1,600 people reached, a majority women; support also included animal husbandry, disease-control and climate-smart agriculture training.
claims.limitations: Programme-reported distribution and training; no comparison group or independent outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: FAO feature, named farmer account from Luumbo Camp in Munyumbwe.
claims.paraphrase: A woman farmer from Luumbo Camp, Munyumbwe, told FAO she had lost livestock in the drought and received replacement goats; the project says a pass-on arrangement is intended to extend offspring to other households.
claims.limitations: One participant account; pass-on extension is an intended design, not a verified community-wide result.

claims.locator: UNICEF story, opening flood impacts and named household account, 30 January 2026.
claims.paraphrase: Late-December 2025 floods in Lundazi and Lumezi submerged Lundazi’s treatment plant, leaving over 40,000 people without safe water; UNICEF describes child displacement, missed school, crop losses and greater illness risk.
claims.limitations: UNICEF field feature; population and service-loss figures are programme-reported, not a district-wide independent assessment.

claims.locator: UNICEF story, response and local-systems paragraphs, 30 January 2026.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reported orienting over 75 community volunteers across four flood-affected health facilities and 11 additional facilities remotely; three hand pumps were provided for installation and three clinic boreholes remained planned.
claims.limitations: Story reports outputs; pump installation and clinic-borehole work are described as planned, not completed.

access_audit.notes: Directly opened and read cited PDF passages; programme achievements are UNICEF annual-reporting outputs.

access_audit.notes: Directly read survey passages; the summary/methods conflict on whether seven or eight districts were sampled, retained as a data limitation.

access_audit.locator: Complete FAO feature page, opening drought context, intervention, sustainability and named farmer paragraphs.
access_audit.notes: Publisher body read directly; participant account and reported project results are identified as such.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNICEF publisher story, flood impacts and response paragraphs.
access_audit.notes: Directly read publisher body; individual household account is illustrative, and planned installations remain prospective.

access_audit.notes: Direct web reader request timed out; its indexed text was not used in claims.

search_audit.query: Zambia 2025 drought district and community vulnerability, children, water access, flood effects and agricultural livelihoods
search_audit.outcome: Read UNICEF's 2025 situation report, eight-district protection survey, FAO's Gwembe/Sinazongwe recovery feature and UNICEF's Lundazi flood account. Local sample and programme limitations are recorded.

search_audit.query: Zambia climate drought water scarcity gender-based violence exploitation child marriage protection risks district evidence
search_audit.outcome: The May 2024 UN appeal explicitly anticipated drought/water-collection-related protection risks and higher child-marriage risk in some unnamed hotspot districts; no measured violent-conflict pathway was directly read.

search_audit.query: Zambia reverse conflict impact climate adaptation, refugee displacement, local insecurity, land or service-access constraints
search_audit.outcome: UNHCR search results suggested climate pressures in refugee-hosting contexts, but direct publisher pages returned cache-miss/429; no named-site conflict or displacement constraint on climate adaptation was verified.

search_audit.query: Zambia local climate resilience and disaster response capacity boreholes social cash transfers and drought-recovery livelihoods 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Read UNICEF response outputs, beneficiary-protection survey, FAO livestock restocking in Gwembe/Sinazongwe and UNICEF flood response in Lundazi/Lumezi; commitments and participant accounts are not treated as independent impact evaluations.

gaps: The directly inspected material offers district-level drought, protection and response detail but limited comparable household vulnerability estimates for individual districts.
The 2024 appeal's gender-based-violence and child-marriage statements are anticipated risks, not measured local incident trends; hotspot districts are unnamed.
UNICEF's beneficiary survey contains a seven-versus-eight district discrepancy, and recipient perceptions are not representative of all drought-affected households.
UNHCR pages relevant to refugee-hosting districts could not be directly accessed (cache miss/HTTP 429); search-result text was excluded, so no climate-to-displacement or reverse pathway is asserted.
No directly inspected source in this collection documented conflict or insecurity impeding climate adaptation in a named Zambian locality.
